name: Northern Yukaghir
notes: Northern (Tundra) Yukaghir, Yukaghir family (an isolate-level branch outside Uralic), Sakha Republic/Chukotka, Russia. INPUT CONTRACT: Tundra Yukaghir Cyrillic orthography, NFC. ⟨ӷ⟩/⟨ӻ⟩ (two attested spellings across sources for the same uvular fricative letter) map to /ʁ/, and ⟨ӄ⟩ maps to the uvular stop /q/ (Maslova 2003 Tundra Yukaghir; NorthEuraLex йоӻул -> j o ʁ u l). ⟨л⟩ is the plain lateral /l/ and ⟨ль⟩ is its palatalised counterpart /lʲ/ — the ordinary Cyrillic hard/soft-consonant convention. An earlier revision of this spec claimed the reverse (⟨л⟩ velarised default /lˠ/, ⟨ль⟩ plain /l/) under a fabricated citation (see the maslova2003tundra source note); corrected on the strength of Schmalz (2013), whose consonant table (Table 2.1.2, pp.30-31) lists only a plain-vs-palatalised /l/~/l’/ contrast with no velarised member, and of NorthEuraLex's own Segments column, which transcribes л as plain [l] (хуруул -> xuruːl) and ль as palatalised [lʲ] (хайль -> xajlʲ) with no exceptions found in the wired gold. Vowel length is spelled by doubling the vowel letter (⟨аа⟩ /a̟ː/, ⟨оо⟩ /o̞ː/, ⟨уу⟩ /uː/, ⟨ии⟩ /ɪː/) — a real length contrast, not free repetition, so the doubled forms are separate keys (Maslova 2003 Tundra Yukaghir). ⟨и⟩ and ⟨е⟩/⟨э⟩ map to the lax /ɪ/ and /ɛ/ phonemes of this inventory (already declared in this spec's ``allophones``, which give [i] and [e] as their open surface variants) rather than to tense /i/ /e/, matching the cited PHOIBLE inventory. ITERATION FIX (error-analysis pass against NorthEuraLex): ⟨ч⟩ maps to the affricate /tʃ/ and the palatalised coronals ⟨нь⟩/⟨дь⟩ to /nʲ/ /dʲ/, Maslova's own transcription convention for Tundra Yukaghir, preferred over this spec's inherited PHOIBLE symbols /c/ /ɲ/ /ɟ/ (a different source's narrower phonetic notation for the same segments); NorthEuraLex evidence (чилгэ 'tʃilge', ньилла 'nʲilla', өдьил 'ødʲil') corroborates the affricate/palatalised-coronal reading. Word stress in Tundra Yukaghir is lexical but is not consistently orthographically marked in the practical Cyrillic script; documented here as an ENGINE-LIMIT stress exemption and not modelled. Classification and coordinates follow Glottolog. GOLD-CONVENTION NOTE (measured, not modelled): NorthEuraLex's Segments column is a broad/simplified IPA transcription that drops the narrow phonetic diacritics this spec's grapheme table carries (advanced [a̟] surfaces in gold as plain [a], lowered [o̞] as plain [o], lax [ɪ]/[ɛ] as tense [i]/[e]) — measured against the wired gold, most of this row's raw mismatches disappear under that one substitution alone, so most of the remaining PER here is notation granularity, not a spec defect; the narrow symbols stay because they are what PHOIBLE 193 and the cited grammars transcribe. Two further patterns are measured but NOT modelled for lack of a source verified this session: (1) the digraph ⟨иэ⟩ (and rarer ⟨ыэ⟩) surfaces in NorthEuraLex as a merged long monophthong [eː] (e.g. чиэмэ -> tʃeːme) rather than this spec's letter-by-letter [iɛ]; Schmalz (2013:27), citing Nikolaeva (2006:30), reports this as one side of a live dispute — Nikolaeva treats /ie/ as a non-phonemic variant of /eː/ while Schmalz argues for a genuine diphthong /ie/ with no /eː/ phoneme — so encoding either the merge or the status quo picks a side of an unresolved phonemic analysis rather than following a settled source; (2) ⟨ы⟩ surfaces in NorthEuraLex as [ɨ] in a handful of forms (былаас -> bɨlaːs) rather than this spec's [ɪ], but Schmalz's vowel inventory (Table 2.1.1, p.26) has no /ɨ/ phoneme at all, so this may be a Russian-loanword reading-rule artifact rather than a native Yukaghir contrast; left unmodelled pending a source that settles it.

sources.author: Maslova, Elena
sources.title: Tundra Yukaghir
sources.publisher: Languages of the World/Materials 372, LINCOM Europa
sources.notes: Grammar sketch of Tundra (Northern) Yukaghir: Cyrillic orthography, ⟨ӷ⟩/⟨ӻ⟩ /ʁ/, ⟨ӄ⟩ /q/, vowel-length spelling by letter doubling, and the lexical-but-unmarked status of stress. This spec previously cited this author/year under the fabricated title "A Grammar of Tundra Yukaghir" attached to DOI 10.1515/9783110197174, which is Maslova's separate Mouton Grammar Library monograph "A Grammar of Kolyma Yukaghir" (Southern Yukaghir, iso639_3 yux) — a different book about a different language. That DOI/title pairing is removed; specific section/page locators from the earlier citation are not carried over because they were never verified against this book's actual text.

sources.author: Schmalz, Mark
sources.title: Aspects of the Grammar of Tundra Yukaghir
sources.notes: Table 2.1.2 (consonant inventory, pp.30-31) gives the lateral series as plain /l/ (coronal) vs. palatalized /l'/ (palatal), with minimal pair tuŋul 'covering' ~ tuŋul' 'patch' (p.26); no velarized lateral allophone or phoneme is described anywhere in the dissertation. NorthEuraLex's Segments column for ykg corroborates this directly: л is transcribed plain [l] (e.g. хуруул -> xuruːl) and ль is transcribed palatalized [lʲ] (e.g. хайль -> xajlʲ), never the reverse.
